name: bigbyte.cc

profile.reading:
123 Central is the name applied to a data center at 123 Central Avenue NW in downtown Albuquerque, New Mexico, operated by bigbyte.cc, a regional colocation and hybrid cloud provider. The building's street number and its marketing name are the same, a detail that suggests the company built its public identity for the facility directly around the address rather than a separate brand name, a common practice among smaller regional colocation operators without the marketing budget of national providers.

On its own website, bigbyte.cc describes the property as a fully hardened secure campus and positions the company as colo-neutral, meaning it does not require customers to use a single upstream network provider and instead offers what it calls complete network redundancy through multi-provider connectivity. The company's service list includes colocation, data center as a service, hybrid cloud enablement, audit and compliance support, disaster recovery and business continuity services, and build-to-suit space for customers with specific requirements, along with scalable office and co-working space, suggesting the building houses more than pure server infrastructure and functions partly as an operations center for tenant staff.

The company's own materials do not publish a total square footage figure, an IT power capacity in megawatts, a tier classification, industry certifications such as SOC or PCI attestations, or a history of the building itself, including when it was constructed or converted to data center use. bigbyte.cc instead directs prospective customers to call a listed phone number for detailed technical specifications, a sales approach typical of regional and privately held colocation operators that compete on service and local relationships rather than on a published specifications sheet aimed at self-service comparison shopping. Albuquerque itself has a modest but real colocation market, serving as a secondary hub along the interstate fiber routes connecting Phoenix, El Paso, and Denver, and a downtown facility positioned to serve New Mexico state government, the University of New Mexico, and contractors tied to Sandia and Los Alamos National Laboratories would be a plausible niche for a locally focused, compliance-oriented operator like bigbyte.cc. Nothing on the company's public site independently confirms that positioning, however, and 123 Central's detailed specifications remain, at this writing, whatever it is prospective customers learn only by contacting the company directly.
profile.research_note: bigbyte.cc's own site (bigbyte.cc) confirms the 123 Central Ave NW Albuquerque address and phone but publishes no IT capacity, sqft, or certification figures for the facility.

reading: bigbyte.cc is a privately held, 100 percent woman-owned data center operator headquartered in Albuquerque, New Mexico, WBENC certified since its founding. The company operates a carrier-neutral colocation and business continuity campus positioned in New Mexico's Innovation Corridor and an Opportunity Zone, marketing its location's access to more than 280 sunny days a year and a regional power grid that sits independent of the Eastern and Western US interconnections, a resilience feature for disaster recovery customers. Third-party data center directories place the facility's capacity at approximately 3 megawatts, a figure this registry records as a lead rather than an operator-confirmed number, since bigbyte's own site emphasizes compliance and service offerings rather than technical specifications. Its target customer base spans small businesses, healthcare, financial and banking, insurance, and government sectors, industries with regulatory compliance requirements that align with the company's stated focus on compliance-driven continuity solutions. bigbyte.cc's colo-neutral model, allowing clients to choose their own service providers rather than bundling connectivity, positions it as a regional single-site alternative to larger wholesale and hyperscale operators elsewhere in this registry, serving a smaller enterprise and regulated-industry customer base in the Southwest.
